title: supabase auth migration: backfill email identities

spec.text: Add a migration that backfills auth.identities for all email-password or email-passwordless (magic link / OTP) users that don't have a corresponding email identity. created_at / updated_at are deliberately hard-coded so the migration can be rolled back by deleting those rows.

context: Postgres, Supabase Auth (GoTrue). New migration, run once per project on upgrade. auth.users.encrypted_password is '' (not null) for users who never set a password: passwordless sign-ins and invited users who haven't accepted yet. A user can already have identities from other providers (google, github, ...). auth.identities: id text, user_id uuid, identity_data jsonb, provider text, last_sign_in_at timestamptz nullable, created_at, updated_at. Client SDKs (gotrue-js and typed ports built from it, e.g. Flutter) declare UserIdentity.last_sign_in_at as a required string.

files.content:
+-- backfill the auth.identities column by adding an email identity 
+-- for all auth.users with an email and password 
+
+insert into auth.identities (id, user_id, identity_data, provider, last_sign_in_at, created_at, updated_at)
+select id, id as user_id, jsonb_build_object('sub', id, 'email', email) as identity_data, 'email' as provider, null as last_sign_in_at, '2022-11-25' as created_at, '2022-11-25' as updated_at
+from auth.users as users
+where encrypted_password != '' and email is not null and not exists(select user_id from auth.identities where user_id = users.id);

source.notes: Diff of commit b54d60a (PR #823) that introduced the migration. Key from follow-up fix migrations: ef1a51f (PR #850, last_sign_in_at left null crashed typed clients) and f7286dd (PR #914, backfill for invited users, matching existing identities on provider = 'email').
